analysis:
The PR adds an optional diagnostic field `coordinatorConnection` (connected, since, connections) to DaemonState. It touches DaemonStateFile.swift (struct, property, init param at head ~lines 88-91, 322-335, 365, 399) and DaemonState+Coding.swift (new CodingKey at line 18, decode at line 51, encode at line 89). The field is optional and decoded with decodeIfPresent, so older state files still decode. The key is additive and the schema stays at 1. The existing comment about the pre-update 0.9.15 watchdog applies: that reader's decoder ignores unknown keys, so it can still validate the heartbeat. Because the custom CodingKeys enum is used, the snake-case key strategy maps coordinatorConnection to coordinator_connection on both read and write, which is consistent.

Security view: the new field carries only a boolean, an epoch timestamp and a counter. It leaks no secrets, keys, prompts or identities (A-001, A-003, A-008 untouched). It is written to the same local diagnostic state file, so existing trust (TB-003) is unchanged. The file is read for diagnostics only. Nothing in this change grants serving authorization (T-052, T-053), and the field is not a trust signal. The change does not touch attestation or the App Attest authorization path (A-016) and does not touch the prefix cache (T-041). The one concern is a local operator forging the field. That has no authorization effect in the visible code, and it is a diagnostic-only display to the same operator.

Limits: the producer that populates the field and the status/doctor consumers are not in the supplied batch. I could not verify whether consumers treat `connected` as an authorization or health gate. The patch excerpt for DaemonStateFile.swift is truncated at the end of the init. The base text of DaemonStateFile.swift was supplied only through line 626, so I examined the visible portion. Nothing visible suggests a security regression.
